faq.q: Is Tsawwassen North an official City of Delta neighbourhood?
faq.a: No. It is a Paragon sub-area name for the north side of Tsawwassen, beside Tsawwassen First Nation lands, planned under the Official Community Plan, Bylaw No. 8400 (2024), and no official boundary exists for the name.

faq.q: Which schools serve the north side of Tsawwassen?
faq.a: It depends on the address. For the sample address 5000 Canoe Pass Way, the SD37 locator result is Ladner Elementary (K–7) and Delta Secondary (8–12), with no middle-school category; catchments are address-based, so check the exact address.

faq.q: What bus runs along the north side?
faq.a: TransLink route 609 runs from South Delta Exchange via 52 Street and Canoe Pass Way through Tsawwassen First Nation to Ladner Exchange, and route 601 serves 56 Street and South Delta Exchange toward Bridgeport Station.

faq.q: Who governs the land beside the north side on Tsawwassen Lands?
faq.a: Tsawwassen First Nation is self-governing, with jurisdiction over land management on Tsawwassen Lands (over 724 hectares under the Final Agreement), so City of Delta zoning does not apply on Tsawwassen Lands.

faq.q: What is the big development on the north side?
faq.a: Tsawwassen Springs, on Springs Boulevard at 52 Street (Shato Holdings with Talisman Homes, developer source), plus a City-listed townhouse project at 4800 Springs Boulevard.
